subject: Discovery recap — migration path off proprietary LLM APIs (MedTech Labs)
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Das <samir@medtechlabs.com>, Catherine Miller <catherine.miller@medtechlabs.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:08:00-05:00
Subject: Discovery recap — migration path off proprietary LLM APIs (MedTech Labs)

Thanks for taking the time today — great discussion. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and immediate next steps. I put action owners in parentheses.

Quick recap of pain points
- Cost volatility with current enterprise OpenAI + Anthropic contracts; monthly spend unpredictable (Samir).
- Latency spikes on critical clinical assistant flows (search + short-completion) — impacts clinician UX (Catherine).
- Data residency & PHI concerns: prefer VPC / on-prem options or strict KMS/HSM controls (Samir).
- Vendor lock-in: desire an exit path from proprietary APIs while maintaining feature parity (function-calling, streaming).

Current stack (as described)
- Primary: OpenAI GPT-4.1 via enterprise API for clinical assist and summarization.
- Secondary: Anthropic Claude for long-form generation workflows.
- Orchestration: in-house request router + prefix cache; uses token-level sampling and rudimentary fallbacks to smaller models.
- Volume: ~800M tokens/mo today across prod + staging; expected 2x growth next 12 months.

Success criteria for a migration/pilot
1) Feature parity: streaming responses, function/tool-calling, and reproducible tokenization for prompts (engineering).
2) Latency: p50 under 200ms for 32–128 token completions in your prod region (us-east).
3) Cost: target total token spend <= current baseline at scale (goal: 20–30% unit token cost reduction).
4) Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence + option for customer-managed keys / VPC deployment.
5) Quality: model outputs must match or exceed current safety and hallucination tolerances on your held prompt set.

Compatibility and technical asks we noted
- Need streaming + incremental token output API (not just batch completion).
- Function-calling semantics and structured JSON output capability.
- Support for shared KV/cache behavior to preserve chat context efficiency.
- Tokenization parity or robust migration tooling for existing prompt templates.

Model shortlist (initial candidates for pilot)
- Llama 3 (server-optimized variant) — good baseline for instruction-following parity.
- Mistral Instruct (7B / 10B) — strong on instruction tuning and cost/latency tradeoffs.
- RedPajama-Chat (incite-derived) — promising safety profile with open weights.
- MPT-30B-Instruct — candidate for longer-form tasks where quality matters more than latency.

Proposed next steps (dates tentative):
- Technical POC: Redwood to run model parity eval on your top 50 prompts + safety checks (action: kimberly – target kickoff 2026-12-09).
- Pilot scope doc + SOW draft: share pilot-scope-v1.xlsx and token estimates (action: rachel – sent 2026-12-05).
- Security/compliance: we will provide SOC 2 artifact bundle and PVN for KMS options; request MedTech SOC 2 questionnaire (action: kimberly).
- Demo & technical deep-dive: schedule 60m session with your infra and security (action: karthik – propose times 2026-12-10 / 12-11).

Please confirm that this aligns with your notes and add anything I missed. If approved, we’ll lock in the POC kickoff next week and share the evaluation plan with runbook and acceptance criteria.

Attachments: pilot-scope-v1.xlsx (scope & milestones), medtech-token-estimates.csv (volume assumptions)

Best,

Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0174

Date: 2026-12-05T16:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — migration path off proprietary LLM APIs (MedTech Labs)

Thanks Kim — concise and accurate. A few clarifications and additional constraints from our side: 
- Monthly volume: closer to 1B tokens if we include anticipated growth from two feature launches in Q1.
- Current spend: ~ $35k/month for prod usage (OpenAI + Anthropic combined) — variability is the main issue.
- PHI requirements: anything touching clinical notes must remain within our VPC or be covered by a BAA + customer-managed keys. We cannot put PHI on a shared public-hosted model without explicit controls.
- Benchmark: we need to see hallucination rates on clinical summarization tasks and safety/regulatory checks for clinical instructions.

Attaching our SOC 2 questionnaire and the clinical prompt set (redacted). Please treat the prompt set as confidential.

Samir
Director of AI Platforms | MedTech Labs
samir@medtechlabs.com
[Attachment: medtech-soc2-questionnaire.pdf]

Appreciate the quick confirmation, Samir — and thanks for the SOC 2 questionnaire. Next up: 

1) Pilot kickoff materials: attached a first-pass SOW and pilot success criteria spreadsheet (pilot-scope-v1.xlsx). This scopes a 6-week technical POC focused on your clinical summarization and triage flows.

2) Technical approach summary (high-level):
   - Redwood will run side-by-side runs of the shortlisted models on your redacted prompt set in a secure sandbox.
   - We’ll measure latency (p50/p95), token costs, and hallucination/safety metrics on our eval harness.
   - For PHI flows we’ll propose either a Dedicated cluster (customer VPC) or an on-prem package — both support KMS/HSM keys.

3) Pricing & contracting timeline:
   - We’ll include a preliminary pilot estimate in the SOW; if the POC meets acceptance criteria we can move to a reserved capacity/Dedicated contract (2–12 month terms).
   - Proposed timeline: SOW sign by 2026-12-10, POC kickoff 2026-12-13.

4) Calendar & action items:
   - Karthish / infra deep-dive: I proposed times in the calendar invite; if those don’t work share preferred windows and we’ll adjust.
   - Rachel will own the evaluation artifacts and run the parity reports (rachel).

Attachments: pilot-scope-v1.xlsx, medtech-soc2-answers-template.docx (for your team to fill)

If that all looks good we’ll set the SOW to send to procurement and include a short procurement checklist for contracts.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly on this.
